target.title: fix(talk): use truncateUtf16Safe for LLM-prompt-facing text truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two LLM-prompt-facing text truncation sites use raw UTF-16 `.slice(0, N)`, which can produce lone surrogates when truncation boundaries cross emoji surrogate pairs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace raw `slice` with the canonical `truncateUtf16Safe` helper:

1. `src/talk/fast-context-runtime.ts` — `normalizeSnippet` truncates memory snippets at 700 chars for realtime response prompts
2. `src/infra/heartbeat-events-filter.ts` — `buildExecEventPrompt` truncates command output at 8000 chars for LLM prompts

## User Impact

None for typical text. Memory snippets or command output that happen to contain emoji at the truncation boundary may previously have produced malformed text in the LLM prompt.

## Evidence

- `truncateUtf16Safe` is the canonical surrogate-safe truncation helper with 18+ dedicated unit tests
- Pattern matches 7 recently merged surrogate-safe truncation fixes by another contributor (#102225, #102266, #102378, etc.)
- No behavior change for ASCII/non-boundary input

**What was not tested**: E2E agent loop with emoji-rich command output at the exact truncation boundary (requires real model inference).
